title: Is Human-Readable Text Necessary for Effective LLM Fine-Tuning?
abstract: arXiv:2609.35868v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Is human readability necessary for effective fine-tuning of large language models? We investigate whether model-conditioned training representations can preserve or improve adaptation utility without requiring a human-readable textual form. We propose Desired-Update-Aligned Synthetic Data (DASA), which uses activation-gradient feedback from a frozen reference model to guide the optimization of continuous synthetic input embeddings. Inspired by the role of activation gradients in local risk reduction, DASA targets useful adaptation updates rather than source-text reconstruction or linguistic fluency. The resulting embeddings are used directly for downstream fine-tuning; discrete token projections are employed only for qualitative inspection. Experiments on six models from the Llama and Qwen families, ranging from 1B to 32B parameters, cover six benchmarks spanning knowledge, mathematical reasoning, code generation, and commonsense reasoni

translated_title: 人类可读文本对于大语言模型的有效微调是否必要？
translated_abstract: 人类可读性对于大语言模型的有效微调是否必要？我们研究了模型条件化的训练表示能否在无需人类可读文本形式的情况下保持或提升适配效用。我们提出了期望更新对齐合成数据（DASA），该方法利用冻结参考模型的激活梯度反馈来指导连续合成输入嵌入的优化。受激活梯度在局部风险降低中作用的启发，DASA 以实现有用的适配更新为目标，而非源文本重建或语言流畅性。所得嵌入直接用于下游微调；离散词元投影仅用于定性检查。在 Llama 和 Qwen 两个系列的六个模型（参数量从 1B 到 32B）上的实验覆盖了知识、数学推理、代码生成和常识推理六个基准测试。
tldr: 提出 DASA 方法，利用冻结参考模型的激活梯度反馈优化连续合成输入嵌入，证明无需人类可读文本也能实现有效的大语言模型微调。
en_tdlr: DASA leverages activation-gradient feedback from a frozen reference model to optimize continuous synthetic input embeddings, demonstrating that effective LLM fine-tuning is possible without human-readable text.
